title: Activation Mosaic: cross-functional canary matrix (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
Sketch for a lightweight, cross-functional canary matrix we can run for LLM features that balances cost/latency safety and behavioral quality. This is intentionally compact — a fieldable checklist + signal mapping that multiple teams (product, SRE, research, solutions) can rally around without heavy ceremony.

High-level idea (one-liner):
Create an "activation mosaic": a small set of orthogonal exposure slices (latency-sensitive, cost-bound, quality-sensitive, geographic/regulatory) and a signal-to-action matrix that maps measured telemetry to deterministic human+automated responses.

Why this instead of a single canary flow?
- LLM features have heterogeneous failure modes: latency spikes, token-cost escalations, semantic drift/hallucinations, content-safety regressions. One axis of traffic doesn't capture multi-dimensional risk.
- Cross-team clarity: each slice owns a primary signal and an escalation path so SRE, product, and ML know what to act on.

Canvas (core components):
- Slices (examples):
  - Slice A: Latency-sensitive (mobile users, short prompts)
  - Slice B: Cost-bound (large-batch embeddings or background inference)
  - Slice C: Quality-watch (prompt templates tied to user-facing responses)
  - Slice D: Safety/Regulatory (EU region, PII-sensitive endpoints)
  - Slice E: Synthetic stress (synthetic traffic for worst-case sequences)

- Primary signals per slice (what we watch first):
  - Latency-sensitive: p95 latency, tail qps per model-worker, CPU/GPU queue depth
  - Cost-bound: per-token cost rate, inference VM utilization per project, sudden increase in avg tokens per request
  - Quality-watch: hallucination rate (eval set comparisons), user feedback rate (thumbs down), rerank degradation
  - Safety/Regulatory: content filter hit-rate, KMS errors, audit-log gaps
  - Synthetic stress: error-rate under synthetic tokens, KV cache eviction rate, memory OOMs

- Secondary signals (context):
  - Traffic mix shift, upstream request size distribution, recent model version rollouts, infra preemption events

Decision matrix (sketch):
- Green (no action): all primary signals within thresholds for 60m
- Amber (investigate, partial mitigation): any primary signal crosses threshold OR 2 secondary signals trend up for 30m
- Red (rollback/backout/fallback): primary signal triggers hard threshold OR multiple slices simultaneously degraded

Automated actions (examples):
- Amber: route 50% of slice traffic to stable model variant; enable lightweight prefix caching; increase sampling for quality telemetry
- Red: immediate fallback to stable model variant + reduce exposure to 0 for slice; page oncall

Human rituals / cross-team runbook steps (minimum viable):
1) Owner assignment: product PM = experiment owner; SRE = infra owner; Research = quality owner; Solutions = customer comms
2) Preflight checklist (24–48h before enabling): confirm telemetry dashboards exist, synthetic replay configured, stash of evaluated prompts available, rollback artifact is validated
3) Activation window: prefer 1–3 hour windows during low global traffic, run a synthetic verification 30m prior to activation
4) Observation cadence: 15m automated pulse checks + 1x manual sweep at 45m
5) Decision checkpoints: at 45m (amber guard), at 120m (long tail evaluation)
6) Post-mortem: within 48h, share to rollout slack channel and update the activation log

Threshold heuristics (examples to standardize across teams):
- Latency p95: +30% above baseline for >10m -> amber; +60% >5m -> red
- Cost rate: sustained +40% token cost vs baseline for >1hr -> amber; +80% immediate -> red
- Hallucination (eval set): relative increase in failure metric >10% absolute points -> amber; >25% -> red
- Safety filter hits: any high-confidence violation for prod user content -> immediate red

Traffic sizing guidance:
- Latency-sensitive: start at 0.1–0.5% of relevant user cohort (mobile app internal beta)
- Cost-bound: can be a higher fraction (1–3%) but limit simultaneous slices to avoid blended cost effects
- Synthetic stress: up to 10% of traffic to a separate synthetic queue (avoid mixing with live users)

Observability checklist (dashboards / alerts):
- Per-slice p95/p99/p50, error-rate, cost-per-request
- Model-level token distribution + avg tokens/request
- KV cache hit ratio and eviction rate
- Safety filter classification counts with sample export
- Rolling sample of generated outputs (R1: manual review, R2: automated eval)

Example queries / metrics (pseudo):
- p95 latency: metric:inference.latency{model:curie-v2,region:us}.p95 by slice
- token cost rate: sum(cost.tokens) / sum(requests) over 1h
- hallucination proxy: 1 - avg(eval.pass_rate) over seeded-eval-suite
(we'll push concrete PromQL once infra people confirm label schema)

Escalation contact map (minimal):
- Oncall SRE: pager (SRE rotation)
- Product PM: Priya Menon
- Research lead (quality): Maya Rodriguez
- Solutions CS lead for affected customers: Liam O'Neill

Pre-signed rollback artifacts:
- pinned model variant id (artifact tag) + validated input-output samples
- automatable circuit-breaker in router config: route to stable model variant key

Simulation & rehearsal plan (fast):
- Day -2: run synthetic stress in isolated env with 10x baseline qps for 1h
- Day -1: run half-scale synthetic test during production low window (observability only, no user exposure)
- Day 0: micro-activation: expose 0.25% of cohort for 2h with full monitoring, runbook in Slack open
- Failure drills: simulate amber -> verify automated mitigation; simulate red -> verify rollback and comms flow

Open questions / decisions to make here (short list):
- Do we centralize slice definitions in Console (recommended) or let each team define their own slices? (tradeoff: consistency vs flexibility)
- How do we store and version the evaluation prompt sets (git + artifact registry vs console-managed)?
- Exact labeling schema for metrics (slice, model_variant, customer_tier) — need eng infra input

Next actions (owners & rough ETA):
- Draft concrete PromQL and dashboard layout (SRE) — ETA: 2025-02-21 — owner: Ethan Cole
- Add activation-mosaic templates to Console exposure UI (product + frontend) — ETA: 2025-03-07 — owner: Priya Menon
- Curate a 150-sample seed eval per customer-segment for quality-watch slice (research) — ETA: 2025-02-28 — owner: Maya Rodriguez
- Run first micro-activation on internal beta cohort (solutions + product) — target week of 2025-03-10 — owner: Liam O'Neill

Notes to self (working):
- Keep the initial matrix intentionally terse — we can expand slice types after 3 successful activations
- Prioritize pre-signed rollback artifacts — they are the cheapest way to reduce blast radius
- Synthetic stress should always run in a separate queue to avoid contamination of user-facing telemetry

Appendix (small templates to copy-paste for activation requests):
Activation request form (short):
- feature name:
- primary slice(s):
- activation window (UTC):
- rollback artifact tag:
- dashboards & alert links:
- point people (product / SRE / research / solutions):
- special notes (PII/regulatory)

Slack channel naming conv: #activation-<feature>-<date>-<owner-short> (keeps ephemeral channels discoverable)

End of sketch. This is intentionally not a fully nailed-down playbook — it's a compact starting artifact to get cross-team alignment and run a few low-risk activations. Will iterate after the first two live runs.
